Runtime Interface (core/shared/types.ts RuntimeInterface: Describe/Health/Capability/Dependency/Need/Reject/Recommend/Explain/Register/Heartbeat/Status/NextAction/Owner/Version/Compatibility) implemented for the Document Engine (engines/documents/selfDescription.ts createDocumentEngineRuntimeInterface()), exposed over app/api/admin/runtime/document-engine?method=X. A 12-section 'Digital Nervous System' mission (Event Bus, Heartbeat, 15-method interface) was narrowed to this — the interface only, pull-based, no event bus/persistent process, since neither exists nor is buildable without new infrastructure in this serverless deployment. Every one of the 15 methods verified by direct invocation with real output (not stubs) before being wired into the API route.

Runtime Self-Describing Contract (19 fields: Identity/Purpose/Responsibilities/Capabilities/Dependencies/Constraints/Health/Current State/Known Problems/Missing Knowledge/Missing Capabilities/Missing Dependencies/Resources Needed/Requested Actions/Execution Scope/Forbidden Scope/Verification Procedure/Success Criteria/Confidence/Last Validation) + Negotiation Flow (BOOT -> Self Announcement -> Runtime Contract -> Knowledge Gap -> Work Request -> AI Execution -> Verification -> State Update -> Registry Commit), as real types in core/shared/types.ts. An 'Architecture Directive' asking for this across ALL ~470 modules with repository-first discovery banned for all future AI sessions was narrowed, by explicit owner choice (AskUserQuestion), to: the type/protocol definitions themselves, plus full implementation for 2 real modules — the Document Engine (upgrading its existing SDRN-P1/P5 SelfDescription) and plugins/drivers/line.ts (chosen for its already-verified real history in KM-002-line). Does not extend to the other ~468 modules or make contract-first mandatory system-wide.

Platform-level Runtime Contract infrastructure: ContextBudget, DeltaContext, WorkOrder, ExecutionReadiness, VerificationContract, MeasurementReport types in core/shared/types.ts (RuntimeNegotiation reused from SDRN-P6's NegotiationFlowState, not duplicated). A 'System-Wide Runtime Execution Platform' directive with mechanical AI-execution gating, real token/read/context measurement, and a 60% numeric acceptance criteria was found to be partially unbuildable in this repository (no persistent process exists to intercept the AI's own tool calls or observe its token usage — that lives in the Claude Code harness, outside this repo) and flagged directly before any build. Owner's custom-scoped answer: build the full type/schema infrastructure and a real Contract Coverage metric, but explicit instrumentation-only (not results-claiming) for the 6 metrics this repo cannot actually observe.

Runtime Context Broker (core/runtime/contextBroker.ts) — promoted SDRN-P7's per-module helper functions (each independently recomputing the full RuntimeContract) into one broker: compute once per module, cache in-process, derive WorkOrder/ContextBudget/ExecutionReadiness/DeltaContext from the same cached instance. Real, instrumented read counter (readCounter, incremented inside both self-description files' real readJSON) enables a genuine before/after measurement (npm run hello -- --broker-report): real repository reads went from 55 (independent recomputation, the actual SDRN-P6/P7 pattern) to 11 (broker, cached) for the same 2-module repeated-access workload — a real, computed 80% reduction, not estimated. Owner instruction: 'Continue after this commit... Promote these computations into the Runtime Context Broker' — treated as a direct continuation of SDRN-P6/P7's already-granted scope (same 2 modules, no new modules, consolidation not expansion) under Rule 105 (Autonomous Architecture Maintenance), not requiring a fresh Plan Lock exception record — logged here for traceability regardless. Serverless constraint disclosed honestly: the cache is in-process only, valid for one execution's lifetime, not persistent across requests (no persistent server process exists in this Vercel deployment, same constraint SDRN-P3/P5 already stated).

Execution Planner + Execution Report — the one genuinely new, buildable subset of a 10-item 'Architecture Upgrade Directive' (Runtime Knowledge Platform), after auditing all 10 items against real state: 3 were already built (Broker/Contract/Delta Context, SDRN-P6/P7/P8), 1 substantially overlapped existing tools (a 'Context Optimizer' duplicating knip/jscpd), and several (Repository Gateway enforcement, a Knowledge Reuse Engine for the AI's own reasoning, Clarification Requests/Preparation Time/Completion Token metrics) were found not achievable in this repository regardless of scope — same reason as SDRN-P7/P8: no access to AI session behavior, only to this codebase's own real data. Owner confirmed the narrowed scope via AskUserQuestion. ExecutionPlan (core/shared/types.ts) extends WorkOrder with one real new field, expectedOutput, derived from the contract's own capabilities/responsibilities. ExecutionReport (core/runtime/contextBroker.ts) aggregates already-real broker data (repositoryReads, knowledgeReused/servedFromCache, contextBudget.skipContext, contract.confidence, contract.requestedActions) into one report per execution — no new computation, no fabricated fields. Verified live for both real modules across a cache-miss and cache-hit access, confirming repositoryReads stays flat and executionTimeMs drops to 0 on the real cache hit.

AI Knowledge Packet completion — owner: 'Transform RuntimePacket into a complete AI Knowledge Packet. AI SHALL execute directly from the packet without reconstructing architectural knowledge.' Treated as a direct continuation under Rule 105 (same 2 modules, no business logic, pure synthesis of already-real data) since it named no new modules and asked for nothing already flagged unbuildable. Found 2 real, closeable gaps in the existing RuntimePacket: (1) an AI reading it still had to cross-reference 6 sub-objects for one picture -> added `briefing` (core/shared/types.ts computeBriefing(), a pure synthesis of contract+readiness fields already present, no new data) (2) module layer + allowed imports existed only as unstructured prose inside contract.constraints, not queryable -> added `architecture` (real lookup against module-registry.json/dependency-graph.json, reusing contract.executionScope[0] as the target file rather than a new registration parameter). Found and fixed a real correctness bug live during this same pass: the first implementation computed architecture unconditionally, adding real file reads even on a cache hit — contradicting the '0 additional reads on cache hit' behavior already verified and logged in SDRN-P8/P9. Fixed by caching architecture alongside the contract; re-verified live (8 reads before and after a cache-hit access, unchanged).
